newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe Gold to merge with Newmont.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe Gold to merge with Newmont.

text.p: Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp said on Monday it had signed a merger agreement with Newmont Mining Corp and had terminated a merger pact with Homestake Mining Co. Newmont said in a statement the merger would create the largest gold company in North America, with 55 million ounces (7.7 million kg) of proven and probable reserves and estimated gold production of 4.0 million equity ounces by 1998.

The agreement with Newmont calls for the exchange of 0.43 share of Newmont for each outstanding share of Santa Fe, Santa Fe said. Previously Newmont had offered an exchange ratio of 0.40, up from its original bid of 0.33.
The merger is subject to approval by shareholders of both Santa Fe and Newmont.
Santa Fe said the merger, which is expected to be tax-free to its shareholders and to be accounted for as a pooling of interests, is expected to close during the second quarter.
Santa Fe said it paid Homestake a termination fee of $65 million, as called for by their merger agreement.

With cash savings from the merger estimated at $70-$80 million a year, and total cash costs in 1998 of about $210 for each ounce of gold produced, Newmont said it expects to be one of the world's most profitable gold producers.
